\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مرفأ} (marfaʾ)}{مرفأ (marfaʾ)}]{\ar{مرفأ} (marfaʾ) — a harbour}

\label{lesson:AR-C430-marfa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to sail, then the Arabic for to dock.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مرفأ}}
\textbf{\ar{مرفأ}} — \emph{marfaʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}a harbour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{قوارب} \ar{الصيادين} \ar{في} \ar{المرفأ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat qawārib aṣ-ṣayyādīn fī al-marfaʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fishermen's boats were in the harbour.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مرفأ}} (\emph{marfaʾ}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{r-f-ʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring a ship close to the shore\textquotedblright{}. The pattern \emph{mafʿal} makes it a place.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marfaʾ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marfaʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat qawārib aṣ-ṣayyādīn fī al-marfaʾ.} — The fishermen's boats were in the harbour.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to sail, then the Arabic for to dock, then say \emph{marfaʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مرفأ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A harbour\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مرسى} (marsā)}{مرسى (marsā)}]{\ar{مرسى} (marsā) — an anchorage; a mooring}

\label{lesson:AR-C430-marsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to dock, then the Arabic for a harbour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مرسى}}
\textbf{\ar{مرسى}} — \emph{marsā} — \textquotedblleft{}an anchorage; a mooring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{وجد} \ar{القبطان} \ar{مرسى} \ar{آمنا} \ar{للقارب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{wajada al-qubṭān marsā āminan li-l-qārib.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The captain found a safe anchorage for the boat.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مرسى}} (\emph{marsā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-s-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be firm, fixed\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the place-noun of \emph{rasā}, \textquotedblleft{}to anchor\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marsā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{marsā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{wajada al-qubṭān marsā āminan li-l-qārib.} — The captain found a safe anchorage for the boat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to dock, then the Arabic for a harbour, then say \emph{marsā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مرسى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An anchorage; a mooring\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{منارة} (manāra)}{منارة (manāra)}]{\ar{منارة} (manāra) — a lighthouse; a minaret}

\label{lesson:AR-C430-manara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a harbour, then the Arabic for an anchorage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{منارة}}
\textbf{\ar{منارة}} — \emph{manāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a lighthouse; a minaret\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رأينا} \ar{ضوء} \ar{المنارة} \ar{من} \ar{بعيد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raʾaynā ḍawʾ al-manāra min baʿīd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We saw the lighthouse's light from far away.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{منارة}} (\emph{manāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}light\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It names a place of light; EtymDB lists Aramaic and Hebrew relatives for a lamp-stand.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raʾaynā ḍawʾ al-manāra min baʿīd.} — We saw the lighthouse's light from far away.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a harbour, then the Arabic for an anchorage, then say \emph{manāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{منارة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lighthouse; a minaret\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{زورق} (zawraq)}{زورق (zawraq)}]{\ar{زورق} (zawraq) — a dinghy; a small boat}

\label{lesson:AR-C430-zawraq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an anchorage, then the Arabic for a lighthouse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{زورق}}
\textbf{\ar{زورق}} — \emph{zawraq} — \textquotedblleft{}a dinghy; a small boat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{خرج} \ar{صياد} \ar{في} \ar{زورق} \ar{قديم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kharaja ṣayyād fī zawraq qadīm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A fisherman went out in an old dinghy.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{زوارق}, \emph{zawāriq}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{زورق}} (\emph{zawraq}) was borrowed from Persian (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{جدف} (jaddafa)}{جدف (jaddafa)}]{\ar{جدف} (jaddafa) — to row}

\label{lesson:AR-C430-jaddafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a lighthouse, then the Arabic for a dinghy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{جدف}}
\textbf{\ar{جدف}} — \emph{jaddafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to row\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{جدف} \ar{أخي} \ar{نحو} \ar{الجزيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jaddafa akhī naḥwa al-jazīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother rowed towards the island.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يجدف}, \emph{yujaddif}.

An oar is \emph{mijdāf}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{جدف}} (\emph{jaddafa}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{j-d-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to row\textquotedblright{}. It is Form II.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[(dialogue)]{Getting around — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R430-review-423-430}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a gate and a seat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a gate, a seat, to reserve, boarding, a runway
  \item to lift off, to land, takeoff, a seat belt, a crew
  \item a flight attendant, a passenger, a destination, to tighten, arrival
  \item customs, to search, to stamp, to empty out, to confiscate
  \item a distance, to make sure, to adjust, to hire, a backpack
  \item a railway, a carriage, a compartment, the metro, to unload
  \item a captain, a boat, a ferry, to sail, to dock
  \item a harbour, an anchorage, a lighthouse, a dinghy, to row
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A gate? (\textbf{\ar{بوابة}}, \emph{bawwāba}.) A seat? (\textbf{\ar{مقعد}}, \emph{maqʿad}.) To reserve? (\textbf{\ar{حجز}}, \emph{ḥajaza}.) Boarding? (\textbf{\ar{صعود}}, \emph{ṣuʿūd}.) A runway? (\textbf{\ar{مدرج}}, \emph{madraj}.) To lift off? (\textbf{\ar{أقلع}}, \emph{aqlaʿa}.) To land? (\textbf{\ar{هبط}}, \emph{habaṭa}.) Takeoff? (\textbf{\ar{إقلاع}}, \emph{iqlāʿ}.) A seat belt? (\textbf{\ar{حزام} \ar{أمان}}, \emph{ḥizām amān}.) A crew? (\textbf{\ar{طاقم}}, \emph{ṭāqam}.) A flight attendant? (\textbf{\ar{مضيف}}, \emph{muḍīf}.) A passenger? (\textbf{\ar{راكب}}, \emph{rākib}.) A destination? (\textbf{\ar{وجهة}}, \emph{wijha}.) To tighten? (\textbf{\ar{شد}}, \emph{shadda}.) Arrival? (\textbf{\ar{وصول}}, \emph{wuṣūl}.) Customs? (\textbf{\ar{جمارك}}, \emph{jamārik}.) To search? (\textbf{\ar{فتش}}, \emph{fattasha}.) To stamp? (\textbf{\ar{ختم}}, \emph{khatama}.) To empty out? (\textbf{\ar{أفرغ}}, \emph{afragha}.) To confiscate? (\textbf{\ar{صادر}}, \emph{ṣādara}.) A distance? (\textbf{\ar{مسافة}}, \emph{masāfa}.) To make sure? (\textbf{\ar{تأكد}}, \emph{taʾakkada}.) To adjust? (\textbf{\ar{عدل}}, \emph{ʿaddala}.) To hire? (\textbf{\ar{استأجر}}, \emph{istaʾjara}.) A backpack? (\textbf{\ar{حقيبة} \ar{ظهر}}, \emph{ḥaqībat ẓahr}.) A railway? (\textbf{\ar{سكة} \ar{حديد}}, \emph{sikkat ḥadīd}.) A carriage? (\textbf{\ar{عربة}}, \emph{ʿaraba}.) A compartment? (\textbf{\ar{مقصورة}}, \emph{maqṣūra}.) The metro? (\textbf{\ar{مترو}}, \emph{mitrū}.) To unload? (\textbf{\ar{أنزل}}, \emph{anzala}.) A captain? (\textbf{\ar{قبطان}}, \emph{qubṭān}.) A boat? (\textbf{\ar{قارب}}, \emph{qārib}.) A ferry? (\textbf{\ar{عبارة}}, \emph{ʿabbāra}.) To sail? (\textbf{\ar{أبحر}}, \emph{abḥara}.) To dock? (\textbf{\ar{رسا}}, \emph{rasā}.) A harbour? (\textbf{\ar{مرفأ}}, \emph{marfaʾ}.) An anchorage? (\textbf{\ar{مرسى}}, \emph{marsā}.) A lighthouse? (\textbf{\ar{منارة}}, \emph{manāra}.) A dinghy? (\textbf{\ar{زورق}}, \emph{zawraq}.) To row? (\textbf{\ar{جدف}}, \emph{jaddafa}.)
